Package eu.cloudhopper.mc.annotations

Annotation Interface EventTrigger

@Retention(SOURCE) @Target(METHOD) public @interface EventTrigger
Declares that the annotated function is invoked for each event from a source such as a queue or a storage bucket.

Use it together with Function. The generator creates the source (unless create() is false) and connects it to the function on the target platform:

EventSource.QUEUE per target
TargetResource
AWSSQS queue
AzureStorage queue in the function app's storage account
GCPPub/Sub topic, delivered through Eventarc
Spring BootPOST /events/<function name>; with spring-kafka and cloudhopper.events.broker=kafka also the Kafka topic of that name
EventSource.STORAGE per target
TargetResource
AWSS3 bucket with an event notification
AzureBlob container in the function app's storage account, delivered through Event Grid and a storage queue
GCPCloud Storage bucket, delivered through Eventarc
Spring BootPOST /events/<function name>

Example


 @Function(name = "orderReceived")
 @EventTrigger(source = EventSource.QUEUE, name = "orders")
 public void onOrder(Order order, EventMetadata meta) {
     // the message body is deserialized from JSON, like an HTTP request body
 }

 @Function(name = "invoiceUploaded")
 @EventTrigger(source = EventSource.STORAGE, name = "invoices")
 public void onUpload(StorageEvent event) {
     // bucket, key and size of the new object; read the content yourself if needed
 }

The function receives one message per invocation. Delivery is at least once: if the function throws, the platform delivers the message again, so the function should tolerate duplicates. A parameter of type EventMetadata receives the message id, source, time, delivery attempt and attributes.

  • Element Details

    • source

      EventSource source
      The kind of event source.
      Returns:
      the event source

    • name

      String name
      The name of the queue (or topic) or bucket the function listens to.

      Use 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, starting with a letter, so that the name is valid on every target. Bucket names on AWS and GCP are global across all accounts: choose a name nobody else uses, for example one that starts with your domain.

      Returns:
      the source name

    • create

      boolean create
      Whether the generator creates the source.

      true (the default) creates it together with the function. false connects the function to an existing source of that name.

      Returns:
      true to create the source
      Default:
      true
